headline: Amazon sought up to 42 billion dollars from bond investors to pay for its AI build, but the filing dates back to March.
score_reason: Pool 7 lowered by 2: the article is from 10 Mar 2026 and was re-dated by Google News, and only its first paragraph is readable.
importance_line: A record-sized borrowing by one of the biggest cloud providers shows how much of the AI build is debt-funded, which matters to bond investors and to the cost of credit for everyone else, but this is a seven-month-old filing resurfacing, not a new sale.
summary: Investor's Business Daily reports, citing an unnamed report, that Amazon filed to sell roughly 37 to 42 billion dollars of bonds in dollars and euros to fund its AI plans; the article itself was first published on 10 Mar 2026 and resurfaced this weekend, so it is not a new sale. Morgan Stanley data relayed by BigGo Finance show Amazon's more recent borrowing was a 4.25 billion pound bond in September.
notes: Re-dated item: page metadata datePublished 2026-03-10. Paywalled after paragraph one. Editor may drop it as stale.
